food.name: Food
food.description: Every day, damage dealt in matches turns into food; the more of the squad plays, the bigger the harvest. It keeps for 7 days before being lost.
food.note: Each point of food carries further the more materials the squad has gathered, by clearing challenges and beating bosses. The town holds on its consumption and grows on its surplus.

foodStock.purpose: What consumption draws from every week, and what raises the population's fed ceiling.
foodStock.caption: Kept for 7 days

consumption.name: Mouths to feed

consumption.purpose: Paid first out of the harvest; what is left over becomes the surplus.
consumption.caption: Eaten every week, whatever happens

surplus.name: Surplus
surplus.description: The week's harvest, once consumption is paid. Never negative.
surplus.purpose: What makes the town grow: the higher it is, the higher the fed ceiling climbs.
surplus.caption: Draws in new inhabitants

efficiency.name: Efficiency
efficiency.description: Every material earned by beating a boss or clearing a challenge raises this factor, with no ceiling.
efficiency.purpose: It multiplies every point of food into feedable inhabitants: the higher it is, the more the same stock feeds.
efficiency.caption: Inhabitants fed per food

materials.purpose: They raise efficiency and step the town up a tier once the next one's threshold is met.

playerProfile.title: Player profile

bonuses.footnote: Regularity adds to your weekly total but does not chip at the boss: it rewards turning up, not output. The squad bonus multiplies a challenge's damage for everyone who cleared it, including those who got there first.
bonuses.regularityLabel: Regularity · days played in the week
bonuses.teamLabel: Squad · multiplier on the challenge's damage
bonuses.title: Regularity & squad

categories.ELITE: Around 105% of a usual week. It asks the squad to push a little harder than usual.
categories.MINOR: Around 65% of the squad's usual week. Usually folded by midweek.
categories.STANDARD: Around 85% of the squad's usual week. One slow week is still recoverable.

boss.description: Every week a boss shows up with a health pool shared by the whole squad. That pool is not a fixed number: it is computed from what the squad actually produced over the recent closed weeks, multiplied by the number of active players. An active player who does not play therefore makes the boss heavier without draining it. Bring it down before Sunday night. The campaign itself only covers the campaign in progress, ten fights: it starts over on the next campaign, without erasing the fights already won.
boss.ladderFootnote: A boss's class does not come out of the draw: it is set by where the week falls in the campaign. Weeks 5 and 10 are the two peaks, each followed by a minor boss to catch a breath. The draw only decides which boss of that class shows up, and no boss ever comes back twice within one campaign.
boss.title: One boss, one shared health bar

calibration.bounds: The reference cannot run away: it stays bounded, so a full stop never makes the boss fall to a single match and a surge never makes it unreachable.
calibration.description: The boss's bar is never set by hand: it tracks the median of what the squad actually produced over the last 4 closed weeks. Play more and the boss grows, ease off and it shrinks. A one-off marathon week does not count, the median ignores it. Calibration moves the size of the fight, never its class: that one is set by the campaign's calendar.
calibration.title: Difficulty that tunes itself

challenges.description: Every Monday, five challenges are drawn from the catalogue, one per difficulty tier. The higher the tier, the more damage it deals to the boss. A challenge does not come back until its whole tier has been cycled through.
challenges.title: Five challenges, one per difficulty

colony.title: The colony
colony.description: You play, that produces food. The food says how many inhabitants the town can feed. Every day, the town moves a little closer to that number. There is no other population rule.

facts.harvest: 85 damage makes 1 food. An average competitive game is therefore worth 5, and that is the barème's damage, already through the day's diminishing returns.
facts.feeds: One food feeds 8 inhabitants to begin with, and more as the town develops. It is the only figure tying food to population.
facts.eats: The town eats population / efficiency a week. The bigger it gets the more it eats, so what is left over melts on its own as it grows.
facts.window: Only the last seven days count. Each day, today enters the tally and the day seven days back leaves it: it is an average, not a reserve.

colony.presence: Everything harvested in a day is multiplied by 1 + (players present / squad size). The whole squad present therefore makes the day count double. A player counts once they have dealt more than 300 raw damage that day, which is one competitive game or three deathmatches: without that threshold, a two-minute deathmatch would be enough to reach the maximum.

damage.description: The mode and outcome of a match set the damage it deals. A ranked win counts for the most, but every match played, won or not, adds to the week.
damage.title: Every match throws a punch
damage.decayLabel: Daily returns · match rank within the day
damage.decayFootnote: Past the fifth match of a day, a match is worth less. A day's matches are ranked from the most to the least rewarding, never in the order you played them, so warming up can never cost your ranked games. Spreading over several days beats doing it all at once.

eligibility.description: One rule, everywhere: a match counts if it was played in a mode the tracker follows, if it played at least one round, if you scored in it, and if it was not a remake. A remake, an abandoned match or an unrecognized queue deals no damage, counts as no active day, and progresses no challenge. It still shows in your history: it was played, it simply does not count towards the week.
eligibility.title: What counts as a played match

night.title: The day
night.description: Every day, the town closes 15 % of the gap between what it holds and what its food allows. There is one ceiling only, so nothing is ever wasted.
night.gap: It moves fast at first and slower and slower after, and never quite arrives. That is deliberate: there is always something left to gain, and never a day where playing is pointless. The other way round, if the food no longer stretches, it falls back at the same speed.
night.moraleFootnote: Morale starts at 50 and depends on bosses alone. It multiplies the climbing speed: at 50 the town closes 7.5 % of the gap a day instead of 15 %. It never slows the fall. The ten fights of a campaign pay 50 morale between them, exactly the room up to the ceiling: a flawless campaign only reaches 100 on its tenth fight, so no boss is ever without effect. At the floor, 3 % a day is left, around 19 % a week: a badly started campaign crawls, but it is never stuck.

progression.description: Some challenges ask not for an absolute threshold but for progress on yourself: beating your own K/D, ACS or headshot rate from the previous 4 weeks by a given percentage. Grinding matches at the same level does not complete them, since the measure is a rate. With no history over the last 4 weeks, the challenge stays out of reach.
progression.title: Progression challenges

ranking.description: Total damage for the week decides the ranking. The rest is glory.

facts.championTitle: 1st place in a finalized week = Champion title, shown on the overview.
facts.crown: The crown stays with the Champion until the next week is finalized.
facts.damage: Weekly ranking: the sum of your damage (matches + challenges + bonuses).
facts.finishingBlow: The finishing blow on the boss is credited separately, in the fight history.

ranking.title: Ranking & crown

town.title: The town
town.description: Gathered materials raise the efficiency: every 150 materials per player, one food feeds one more inhabitant. There is no threshold to cross and no maximum: a validated challenge makes the food carry further that same Monday, and one validated in the last week is worth exactly what one from the first was.
town.bossMaterialsLabel: Materials per defeated boss, per player
town.materialsLabel: Materials per validated challenge, per player
town.tiersFootnote: A defeated boss pays its materials to every squad player, never inhabitants: inhabitants would fade at 15 % a day, whereas efficiency never comes back down. Materials are divided by the squad size before being converted, which keeps the balance identical from 2 players to 20. A regular campaign runs from 8 to 16 efficiency, one tier a week.

colony.claim: A campsite at the start, a city if the campaign holds. *All of it comes from real matches.*
colony.title: The town is the score

intro.claim: Every match is read automatically, and grows a colony *the whole squad* shares.
intro.title: Your matches build a town

ladder.claim: Food spoils in seven days. Materials, *never*: they carry every harvest further.
ladder.title: From a match to an inhabitant

players.claim: Rank, history, K/D, headshots, personal bests. *Match by match*, from day one.
players.title: Every player has a profile

ranking.claim: Everything resets on Monday. Whoever leads a closed week keeps the *Champion* crown.

week.claim: Its health bar is *sized against your real weeks*. The group plays more, the boss grows.
